NEW SECTION . 146F.2 Dispensing of abortion-inducing 15 drugs —— restrictions. 16 1. A person shall not dispense an abortion-inducing drug in 17 this state unless all of the following criteria are met: 18 a. The drug is dispensed in a health care setting directly 19 to the woman prescribed the drug. 20 b. The person dispensing the drug is authorized to do so 21 pursuant to section 147.107. 22 2. Section 144.29A, subsection 7, paragraph c, Code 7 2026, is amended to read as follows: 8 c. “Spontaneous termination of pregnancy” , commonly known 9 as a miscarriage, means the occurrence of an unintended 10 termination of pregnancy at any time during the period from 11 conception to twenty weeks gestation and which is not a 12 spontaneous termination of pregnancy at any time during the 13 period from twenty weeks or greater which is reported to the 14 department as a fetal death under this chapter . 15 EXPLANATION 16 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 17 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 18 This bill relates to abortions, including informed 19 consent, dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs, and reporting 20 abortion-inducing drug complications. 21 DIVISION I —— ABORTION DEFINED. The bill excludes 22 a spontaneous termination of pregnancy, if not all the 23 products of conception are expelled, from the definition of 24 abortion for the purpose of the reporting requirements and 25 penalties on abortions under Code chapter 146B (abortion —— 26 postfertilization age). 27 DIVISION II —— INFORMED CONSENT. Under the bill, a 28 physician, prior to performing or attempting to perform an 29 abortion, is required to perform an in-person examination of 30 the woman seeking an abortion, including screening for indicia 31 of coercion or abuse; if necessary, the physician shall make a 32 referral to an appropriate health care provider consistent with 33 the examination results. 34 The bill requires a physician who is performing or 35 -8- LSB 5778YC (8) 91 ak/ko 8/ 11 H.F. _____ attempting to perform a chemical abortion, prior to prescribing 1 or dispensing an abortion-inducing drug, to do all of the 2 following: have the woman being prescribed or dispensed the 3 drug sign a patient agreement form, obtain written confirmation 4 that the physician has informed the woman of specific health 5 and safety information related to abortion-inducing drugs 6 as detailed in the bill, and advise the pregnant woman how 7 to access emergency surgical intervention in cases of an 8 incomplete abortion, severe bleeding, or other medical 9 complications. The bill specifies that these requirements 10 shall not apply to a chemical abortion performed in response to 11 a medical emergency. The bill provides that the prohibition on 12 dispensing of abortion-inducing drugs shall not be construed 13 to impose civil or criminal liability on a woman upon whom 14 a chemical abortion has been performed. Under the bill, 15 a physician who fails to comply with the informed consent 16 requirements is subject to licensee discipline. The bill 17 requires the board of medicine to adopt rules to administer 18 this division of the bill. The bill defines “abortion-inducing 19 drug”, “chemical abortion”, “dispense”, “medical emergency”, 20 and “pregnant” or “pregnancy”. 21 The bill requires the department of health and human 22 services (HHS) to publish on HHS’s internet site notice that it 23 may be possible to reverse the effects of a chemical abortion, 24 and information and resources on reversing the effects of a 25 chemical abortion. 26 DIVISION III —— DISPENSING AND REPORTING —— 27 ABORTION-INDUCING DRUGS. The bill defines “abortion-inducing 28 drug”, “abortion-inducing drug complication”, “chemical 29 abortion”, “dispense”, “interested party”, “medical emergency”, 30 “physician”, “postfertilization age”, and “rural emergency 31 hospital”. 32 The bill prohibits a person from dispensing an 33 abortion-inducing drug in this state unless the drug is 34 dispensed in a health care setting directly to the woman 35 -9- LSB 5778YC (8) 91 ak/ko 9/ 11 H.F. _____ prescribed the drug, and the person dispensing the drug is 1 authorized to do so pursuant to Code section 147.107 (drug 2 dispensing, supplying, and prescribing —— limitations). These 3 requirements do not apply to a medical emergency. 4 The bill requires a hospital, rural emergency hospital, 5 or the attending physician to file a report with HHS using a 6 prescribed form within 30 days of discharge or death of a woman 7 who presented with or was treated for an abortion-inducing 8 drug complication. The form must be signed and completed 9 by the attending physician and contain the age of the woman 10 experiencing the abortion-inducing drug complication, 11 the woman’s state and county of residence, the date the 12 abortion-inducing drug was used by the woman, and the probable 13 postfertilization age of the unborn child at the time of 14 the abortion-inducing drug complication. The report must 15 identify the physician who performed the chemical abortion, 16 the facility where the chemical abortion was performed, 17 the referring physician, agency, or service, if any, and 18 the specific complication or complications that led to the 19 treatment performed along with the most recent international 20 classification of diseases code for each, if applicable. The 21 report shall be confidential and not subject to disclosure 22 under Code chapter 22 (open records). 23 The bill also requires HHS to prepare annually on or 24 before December 31 a comprehensive statistical report based 25 upon the aggregated data gathered from the reports filed on 26 abortion-inducing drug complications. Under the bill, the data 27 gathered by HHS must be anonymized to prevent public disclosure 28 of either the physician or hospital that filed a report, or the 29 woman about whom a report is filed. HHS is required to make the 30 anonymized data publicly available in a downloadable format on 31 its internet site. 32 This division of the bill creates a private cause of action 33 against any person who dispenses an abortion-inducing drug 34 in violation of this division of the bill for all damages 35 -10- LSB 5778YC (8) 91 ak/ko 10/ 11 H.F. _____ caused by the abortion-inducing drug suffered by a woman upon 1 whom a chemical abortion was performed or was attempted or 2 the personal representative of the woman upon whom a chemical 3 abortion was performed or was attempted. The bill defines 4 “personal representative” as an administrator or an executor, 5 or if there is no such personal representative appointed, 6 then a person legally authorized to perform substantially the 7 same functions. A prevailing plaintiff in an action brought 8 under this division of the bill, in addition to compensatory 9 and punitive damages, is entitled to statutory damages in the 10 amount of $50,000, court costs, and reasonable attorney fees. 11 In an action brought under this division of the bill, the name 12 and other identifying characteristics of a woman who sought or 13 obtained an abortion-inducing drug shall be redacted from all 14 pleadings and documents filed in the action without a court 15 order, and the court may make further orders as necessary to 16 protect the identity and privacy of the woman who sought or 17 obtained an abortion-inducing drug. This division of the bill 18 is not to be construed to impose civil or criminal liability 19 upon a woman upon whom a chemical abortion is performed. 20 Under the bill, a licensee that fails to comply with this 21 division of the bill is subject to licensee discipline. 22 DIVISION IV —— ABORTION-RELATED PROVISIONS. The bill amends 23 Code section 144.29A (termination of pregnancy reporting —— 24 legislative intent) to require a health care provider that 25 diagnoses or induces a spontaneous termination of pregnancy 26 to include in the required report to HHS if mifepristone or 27 misoprostol was used to induce a spontaneous termination of 28 pregnancy. Current law requires the health care provider to 29 only disclose if mifepristone was used to induce a spontaneous 30 termination of pregnancy. The bill also requires the health 31 care provider to disclose whether mifepristone or misoprostol 32 were ingested by the patient within 14 days prior to the 33 spontaneous termination of pregnancy. 34 -11- LSB 5778YC (8) 91 ak/ko 11/ 11
